patch_description: The current program builds a greedy schedule from each starting transaction. Greedy construction alone is myopic — it cannot repair ordering mistakes made early. A classic improvement is to follow each greedy construction with a local search: repeatedly try swapping pairs of transactions in the sequence (prioritizing swaps of nearby positions and swaps involving conflicting transactions, since makespan only changes when dependency order of conflicting txns changes), accepting any swap that reduces makespan. Iterating this until no improving swap exists typically shaves significant makespan off greedy solutions. We keep multiple restarts (one per starting transaction plus randomized restarts) and apply local search to each, returning the best. This directly minimizes the true objective (evaluated via get_opt_seq_cost) rather than heuristics, which the prompt warns against.
